title: Generate spritesheets and animations for your game with Gamelab Studio
author: macuseri686
selftext:
I’ve been experimenting heavily with agentic coding + generative workflows while building my own vanilla HTML Canvas tower-defense game (Age of Steam Tower Defence [https://www.crazygames.com/game/age-of-steam-tower-defence](https://www.crazygames.com/game/age-of-steam-tower-defence) ), and the biggest bottleneck was always **assets:** different angle sprites, animations, variations, packaging, etc.

So I built **GameLab Studio** ([https://gamelabstudio.co](https://gamelabstudio.co)):  
an AI-integrated tool that plugs directly into **Cursor or VS Code** via MCP, or you can use the studio platform online.  
  
You can:

* Generate art, sprites, and animations *directly in your code editor*
* Auto-create multi-angle spritesheets for characters, towers, VFX, etc.
* Drop assets straight into your project folder without context switching

https://preview.redd.it/br8pib5nd15g1.png?width=5760&format=png&auto=webp&s=c16a8ea628d039a7350547f6ec93f76331c7a8ab

https://preview.redd.it/ldojemv6d15g1.png?width=1200&format=png&auto=webp&s=d9a448f16a6bc33aea183e3f636790cfe8b653f5

It’s designed for solo devs and indie teams who want to move fast without getting buried in asset production.

If you’re experimenting with AI-assisted game development, I’d love feedback or feature ideas. Happy to answer questions!

comments.author: Jewish_Coin
comments.body: Nano banana pro exists, man. Does this do anything better?

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body:
Yes, actually. So, nano banana pro is probably one of the best image generation models out there, but its just a model. Its not going to give you transparency, or animations, and it cannot generate spritesheets. It is also limited to certain resolutions.

GameLabs Studio is the full workflow for generating your game assets from start to spritesheet, while maintaining coherence between each of the views of your subject, and each different animation sequence. Gamelabs Studio also keeps your project organized, grouping resources by project, and asset, and view angle.

You can also use Gamelabs Studio directly in your codded editor agent, by connecting the MCP server and simply asking the agent to generate the assets and animations you need for a given unit.

replies.body: Thank you for trying the tool and reporting the issue! comments.author: alexor1976
comments.body: I’m on the fence about subscribing but it misses a few feature , will it be possible at some point to control the number of frame we want  before generating 4s!( i mainly need 1-2s loops with no framerate for walk cycles)

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body:
Hi alexor1976, it is currently possible to control the number of frames to generate for the spritesheet. Number of frames is calculated by fps \* duration in seconds. So to set 20 frames, you could set fps 20 and duration 1s, or like fps 10 and duration 2s etc. 

You can set an arbitrary frame rate in your game engine. The frame rate here just determines the sampling rate of the animation that gets extracted to the spritesheet
